analysis:
The only change in this batch is a documentation edit to docs/architecture/inference.md at line 1846, the `stop` row of the sampling-parameter table. It now describes scoped stop-string matching: GPT-OSS limits matching to the Harmony `final` message via `ModelEOSPolicy.stopStringScope`; Gemma 4 and `<think>` parsers exclude reasoning and tool-call spans per request via `ReasoningStopScope`; the native block engine matches the whole output. The rest of the head text in both units (lines 1612-2420) is unchanged context. I checked it against the canonical threat model and found no new attack surface or control change in the supplied evidence.

The edit alters no code, key handling, attestation, coordinator-provider encryption or cache storage. It is a doc-only description of existing or intended source behavior, so it neither weakens nor invalidates TB-002, TB-007 or T-041. The prefix-cache and SSD text in the surrounding context is unchanged. Its statement that sampler/stop settings are not part of cache identity predates this PR.

I cannot verify from this batch that the described scoping (`StopHoldback`, `ReasoningStopScope`, `ModelEOSPolicy.stopStringScope`) exists in the Swift source as documented. If it does not, the result is a documentation accuracy issue, not a security regression. A consumer-supplied stop string matching inside reasoning or tool-call spans could affect output integrity or tool-call truncation, but that is functional behavior within the consumer's own request. The corresponding code files were not supplied, so integration should confirm only that the documentation matches the implementation. I do not claim a full audit.
